correctness.rationale: Complete proof from exact 12-facet and 24-edge incidence of the rhombic dodecahedron and exact 12-edge cube incidence, followed by exhaustive two-chamber sign analysis under signed permutations. Independent rational vertex/facet/edge checker confirms each face and each edge. Girard's spherical-excess calculation determines the Haar probability exactly. Monte Carlo is corroborative only, not the proof. Degenerate measure-zero normals are excluded by explicit quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The pointwise relation between section-vertex counts of two distinct canonical solids, \(N_C(u)+N_R(u)=12\), is a new geometric incidence comparison relative to the inspected primary cube treatment; its explicit rhombic-dodecahedral marginal and full cooriented joint law are not entailed by a cube-only probability formula without the additional twenty-four-edge case analysis. Database searches for the relation, its symmetry-chamber alias, and the numerical marginal did not locate a dominating published result. Priority remains provisional because some older stereological and crystallographic literature was not fully examined.
residual_risks: Older stereological or crystallographic section-classification literature may contain the same pointwise pairing; searches and accessible primary comparisons do not certify global historical uniqueness.
The published rectangular-box record was accessible by title and summary but not by complete full text; ancillary geometric remarks are unknown.

The result extends a classical elementary cube problem; some readers may regard the new companion-solid identity as a short geometric corollary, but the value claim is the complete cooriented two-solid section classification, not the known numerical constant.

value.rationale: The joint type law and pointwise 12-vertex complementarity classify central sections of two different canonical space-filling polyhedra in one shared direction; the rhombic-dodecahedral octagon majority is a natural exact stochastic-geometric invariant of the canonical Voronoi cell. The result is structural and complete on its natural domain, not just a numerical recomputation of the cube formula. A full general-polytope theorem is neither claimed nor necessary.
